**Grant Application: Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) for CalVIP Funding**

Sacramento’s communities of color bear a disproportionate burden of gun violence, necessitating culturally competent and engaging safety interventions. Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) is a minority-owned social enterprise dedicated to empowering these communities through vital gun safety education. We urgently seek $500,000 from the CalVIP program to expand our innovative, community-rooted initiatives, directly addressing this critical public health and safety crisis.

Our programs are designed for maximum impact and reach. The "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP leverages relatable storytelling to educate youth on responsible gun interaction and avoidance in an age-appropriate manner. Complementary AI education equips participants with future-ready skills, fostering critical thinking relevant to safety and digital literacy. Hands-on community workshops, often hosted in partnership with the trusted Church of Legacy, provide practical, life-saving knowledge on safe storage, conflict de-escalation, and firearm awareness for all ages.

These programs will yield measurable outcomes: a significant increase in gun safety knowledge among participants, a reduction in accidental shootings involving youth, and the cultivation of safer, more resilient communities. GAFC is uniquely qualified due to our deep community roots, minority-owned status ensuring cultural competence and trust, and our innovative blend of traditional education with modern media. Our strong partnership with the Church of Legacy demonstrates established community engagement and a proven ability to deliver impactful, relevant programming where it's needed most. We are ready to scale our efforts to save lives.
